we_do_better: Techniques vs. tools distinction — we separate reusable methods (Skills) from products (Tools), which no competitor does; this is uniquely valuable for practitioners
Source transparency — video quality badges, low-quality flags, and endorsement counts let users judge credibility at a glance; competitors show no provenance
MCP/connector tracking — dedicated Connectors tab covering MCP servers is a niche no competitor addresses
Live RSS news feed merged with video-sourced news, covering 50+ authoritative AI sources alongside the playlist
Self-improvement system and open audit trail (merge log, deleted skills, suggestion queue) — competitors are static catalogs that never explain their curation choices
Fully free, open-source, no ads, no paywall
they_do_better: Visual thumbnails and tool logos — Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, and Toolify show product images; our wall of text cards is harder to scan quickly
Item-count badges per category — Future Tools and TAAFT display count per filter tab; users immediately know scope before clicking
Simultaneous multi-axis filtering — Toolify lets users filter by category + pricing + rating at once; we only support category filter per tab
Hero section and featured/trending slots — all four competitors surface a 'start here' section; we drop visitors into an unlabelled card list
Sort controls — competitors offer newest / top-rated / most-popular sort; our Skills and Tools tabs only sort by quality score with no user control
User-generated signals — Product Hunt shows upvotes and comments; TAAFT shows verified-user saves; our popularity is editorial (video endorsement counts), not crowd-sourced
borrow_next: Add item-count badges to tab buttons (e.g. 'Skills (10)', 'Tools (50)') — one line of JS per tab, high discoverability signal at zero cost
Add a sort toggle (Quality | Mentions | Newest) to the Skills and Tools tabs — ~15 lines of JS, eliminates the main gap vs Toolify/Future Tools for power users

Add a 2-sentence 'What is Excavatortron?' tagline beneath the H1, and pin the top-3 starred skills to the top of the Skills tab as a 'Featured' strip — teaches new visitors what they're looking at without a tutorial

findings.detail: TODAY = datetime(2026, 6, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc) is hardcoded at module level. The recency penalty function compute_age_months() subtracts video age from this frozen date, so all recency penalties calculated after June 3 2026 are wrong — videos will appear progressively older than they are, inflating penalties and depressing quality scores over time.
findings.suggestion: Replace with datetime.now(timezone.utc) (computed inside compute_age_months or at call time, not module level), exactly as src/fetch.py does.

findings.detail: load_json and save_json open files without encoding='utf-8'. Hebrew transcripts and Unicode tool names (common in this playlist) will cause UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 default-locale runners. src/fetch.py uses encoding='utf-8' consistently; analyze_batch.py does not.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to every open() call in load_json (line 152) and save_json (line 160).

findings.detail: "Anthropic" is catalogued as a tool (6/10, 73× mentions) with the description "Anthropic is an AI tool by Anthropic. It enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation." Anthropic is the company, not a product. Its tool-card is misleading and inflates the tools count with a non-tool entry.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'anthropic' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into the 'claude' tool entry (Anthropic's product). Add to improvement_suggestions.json as a safe_auto merge.

findings.detail: "Openai" is catalogued as a tool (6/10, 45× mentions) with the same generic description. OpenAI is the company; its relevant products (ChatGPT, DALL-E, GPT-4) already have their own entries. Having 'openai' as a separate tool creates confusion and duplicate credit.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'openai' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into 'chatgpt'. Raise a suggestion for the improve stage to auto-merge.

findings.where: data/tools.json — top 10 entries by mention count
findings.detail: At least 6 of the top 10 most-mentioned tools share an identical description template: 'X is an AI tool by Y. It enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation.' The most-mentioned tool (Claude, 396×) has this filler description. This is the first thing new visitors see and it destroys trust.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage should regenerate descriptions for all tools whose description matches the template pattern 'enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation'. These are low-value auto-generated strings that should be replaced with one-sentence factual descriptions from the actual transcripts.

findings.detail: 52 news entries (1 daily + 22 weekly + 29 monthly) have empty summaries, causing the UI to show '(summary pending)' — which reads as a pipeline failure to users. These are older videos that were classified before the summary-fill logic ran.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries safe_auto module should back-fill these from the stored transcript/description. As a quick win, a one-pass script can fill them from the pending records or existing processed records.

findings.detail: MCP connector detection uses a hardcoded list of only 8 specific string patterns (filesystem, browser, github, postgres, sqlite, memory, slack, google drive). Any other MCP server mentioned in a video — including custom, Smithery-hosted, or community servers — is silently ignored. CLAUDE.md Step 8 specifies exhaustive MCP hunting; the batch analyzer provides almost none.
findings.suggestion: Broaden detection: capture any pattern matching 'npx .+-mcp', 'uvx .+-mcp', 'mcpServers', 'smithery', or 'mcp.so' in the text as a generic MCP connector, extracting the name from the matched string. Append detected connectors with fields derived from context rather than a static lookup table.

findings.detail: Slash-command regex r'/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,20}\b' matches URL path segments (/api, /v1, /s3), common prose slashes, and file paths. The exclusion list (line 601) only blocks 14 single-character tokens. Over a playlist of 900+ videos this will accumulate false-positive commands in commands.json.
findings.suggestion: Add a context requirement: only record a slash command if it appears adjacent to known AI tool names (Claude Code, claude, /terminal) or follows a clear command-demonstration phrase ('run /...', 'type /...', 'use the /... command'). Also extend the blocklist to common path prefixes (/api, /v1, /v2, /src, /static, /docs).

findings.detail: The tool is stored as "Chatgpt" (wrong casing) instead of the correct brand name "ChatGPT". This is the 3rd most-mentioned tool and the casing error appears in the dashboard for every visitor.
findings.suggestion: Rename name to 'ChatGPT' and update slug to 'chatgpt' (slug already correct). One-line fix in data/tools.json.

findings.detail: fetch_playlist_videos calls request.execute() with no retry or error handling for YouTube API quota exhaustion (HttpError 429/503). If the quota is hit mid-pagination (playlist has 976 items across ~20 pages), the function raises an unhandled exception and the entire fetch run fails, leaving all new videos un-fetched until the next cron.
findings.suggestion: Wrap request.execute() in a retry loop with exponential backoff for 429/503, up to 3 attempts, before re-raising. The googleapiclient library provides MediaUploadError/HttpError with .resp.status for this check.

findings.detail: The most-mentioned tool (Claude, 396×) is shown with a generic template description as the first card on the Tools tab. The highest-traffic entry in the catalog communicates no actual information about Claude.
findings.suggestion: Fix the source data (replace template descriptions) AND add a UI guard: if a tool description matches the known template pattern, show a 'Description pending' pill instead of the filler text to signal incompleteness rather than false completeness.

findings.detail: Tab buttons show no item count. Competitors (Future Tools, TAAFT) display per-category counts that give visitors an immediate sense of catalog scale and density before clicking. Absence makes the tabs feel like placeholders.
findings.suggestion: After loading each tab's data in the init() async block, inject item counts into the nav buttons: e.g. 'Skills (10)', 'Tools (50)', 'Connectors (7)'. ~10 lines of JS.

findings.detail: Skills and Tools tabs have no sort control. Users can only filter by category; they cannot sort by newest, by mentions, or reverse quality order. All four benchmark competitors offer multi-axis sort.
findings.suggestion: Add a sort <select> or pill-toggle above the card list: Quality (default) | Mentions | Newest. Implement as a client-side sort on the already-loaded array — no extra fetch needed. ~20 lines of JS.

findings.detail: No hero tagline or onboarding copy explains what Excavatortron is. First-time visitors see 'Excavatortron — AI Skills Tracker' and then a search box and cards with no context. All four competitors have a 2-3 sentence value proposition above the fold.
findings.suggestion: Add one sentence beneath the subtitle: 'Tracks AI techniques, tools, models, and MCP connectors extracted from a curated YouTube playlist — updated automatically, quality-scored, and searchable.' Costs zero developer effort, permanently fixes first-impression clarity.

findings.detail: Inline Python in both workflows uses datetime.datetime.utcnow() which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and will emit DeprecationWarning. When GitHub Actions upgrades the ubuntu-latest Python to 3.13+, this may become a hard error.
findings.suggestion: Replace datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' with datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() in both workflow inline scripts.

findings.detail: renderAlert builds el.innerHTML = msg where msg contains raw HTML tags hardcoded in JS alongside esc(status.token_hint). The esc() call protects the dynamic value, but the pattern (mixing safe-markup with partially-escaped content) is fragile — a future maintainer adding another dynamic field may forget esc() and introduce stored XSS. Data comes from repo-committed JSON (low external risk), but the pattern is worth fixing.
findings.suggestion: Build the alert using DOM methods (createElement, textContent) rather than innerHTML, or create a dedicated safe-template function that always escapes dynamic values and keeps static HTML separate.

top_actions: Fix the hardcoded TODAY date in src/analyze_batch.py:20 — it corrupts all recency penalty calculations for new videos after June 3 2026. One-line fix with high correctness impact.

Replace the 6+ generic template tool descriptions ('enhances productivity through AI-powered features and automation') for the top-mentioned tools — these are the first entries visitors see and they destroy credibility. Particularly Claude (396×), ChatGPT (110×), and Gemini (52×).

Remove 'anthropic' and 'openai' as separate tool entries — they are companies, not products, and their mention counts inflate the tools catalog with misleading non-tools. Merge their endorsement_video_ids into 'claude' and 'chatgpt' respectively.
Add encoding='utf-8' to all open() calls in src/analyze_batch.py — Hebrew transcripts already in the pipeline will cause silent UnicodeError failures on non-UTF-8 runners.
Back-fill the 52 empty news summaries via the improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module — '(summary pending)' in the news feed looks like a broken pipeline to users.
